features.title: KVM for the VM target: research, VM tools in the dev container, and the vm-host-check recipe
features.description: Settles the open question 'KVM on the hosts'. `docs/findings/F150.md`, headed `## F150`, reports with commands and their output: whether the dev container (`harness/Containerfile`, started by `harness/run.sh` under rootless podman) can open `/dev/kvm`, whether the host has it and with what permissions, and what exactly would expose it to the container (for example a `--device /dev/kvm` in `harness/run.sh` and a group); and whether a GitHub-hosted Linux runner (the `ubuntu-26.04` runner the E2E workflow uses) offers KVM and what a job must do so the runner user may open `/dev/kvm` (verified by a run, or inferred from GitHub's documentation, marked as such). It measures nothing with software emulation unless a person asks. It ends with a line `Decision: ` naming the change for the dev container and for CI. A change to the host is a person's: if one is needed the builder writes `BLOCKED.md` with the options; a builder never switches to software emulation. Indexed in `docs/findings.md`. Then, as the finding decides: The dev container (`harness/Containerfile`) installs, from the distribution and with a comment saying why, what the VM target needs that it lacks: `qemu-system-x86` (with `qemu-utils`), the OVMF firmware (`ovmf`), the NoCloud seed tool (`cloud-image-utils` for `cloud-localds`, or the ISO tool the boot of F151 settles on), and the Ubuntu cloud image signing key (`ubuntu-keyring`, `/usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-cloudimage-keyring.gpg`) for `gpgv`; `swtpm` is already there. `harness/run.sh` exposes `/dev/kvm` to the container as the finding decided. A new recipe `just vm-host-check` (`scripts/vm-host-check.sh`) checks each requirement of the VM target (KVM openable by the current user, `qemu-system-x86_64`, the OVMF code and vars files, `swtpm`, the seed tool, `gpgv` and the keyring) and fails naming each one missing; it never offers software emulation. Its self-test `scripts/test-vm-host-check.sh` (stubbed paths, a negative control per requirement) joins `just test-scripts`. Rebuilding the dev container is a person's step: once the Containerfile and `run.sh` change is committed, the builder writes `BLOCKED.md` asking for the rebuild, and the feature passes on the rebuilt container.
features.verify: f=docs/findings/F150.md && grep -q '^## F150' "$f" && for w in '/dev/kvm' 'harness/run.sh' 'runner' 'ubuntu-26.04' 'udev'; do grep -qF -- "$w" "$f" || exit 1; done && grep -qE '\*\*(verified|inferred)\*\*' "$f" && grep -qE '^Decision: ' "$f" && grep -qF '(findings/F150.md)' docs/findings.md && just quick && scripts/test-vm-host-check.sh && just vm-host-check

features.title: Research: booting the Ubuntu 26.04 minimal cloud image with swtpm, tpm-crb and OVMF

Records the boot that Design 1 relies on, done by hand in the dev container with KVM (the research may boot the VM; it records every command it ran). `docs/findings/F151.md`, headed `## F151`, gives: where the image and Ubuntu's signed checksums (`SHA256SUMS`, `SHA256SUMS.gpg`) are published, how the serial is read, and how long old serials stay on the mirror (input to the pinning choice); the QEMU command line (KVM, OVMF code and vars, `-tpmdev emulator` with `tpm-crb`, `swtpm` socket and state directory); that the guest kernel has `CONFIG_TCG_CRB=y` and `/dev/tpmrm0` appears; `systemd-analyze has-tpm2` before and after installing `libtss2-rc0t64` without recommends; the systemd and kernel versions in the guest; the channel the harness drives the guest over without any change to the product (SSH on user networking with a key from the NoCloud seed, or a serial or virtio console), with its setup; that apt reaches the archive (the image ships empty apt lists); and that a guest power cycle with the `swtpm` state kept keeps the TPM's persistent state. features.title: Research: making the virtual TPM lack a capability RSA 2048 needs
features.description: Settles the open question 'How to make the virtual TPM lack an RSA capability'. `docs/findings/F152.md`, headed `## F152`, tries the candidate routes in the VM of F151 (booting by hand, commands recorded): M4's `tpm-filter` (`custodio-it` example) placed between QEMU's emulator backend and `swtpm` (control channel and data channel); an `swtpm`/`libtpms` profile that disables an algorithm, with the `swtpm` version that supports it and how the dev container and CI would get it; and any other route found. For each route that works it shows, in the guest: the capability missing as every guest process sees it (kernel, `systemd-creds`, the service's capability query of F107/F111 in `docs/api.md`, `tpm2-tools`); that the kernel's TPM (`/dev/tpmrm0`, any primary it makes for bus encryption) and `systemd-creds` sealing with 'host plus TPM' still work; that the service's ECC P-256 parent can still be created; and whether P-256 can also be made to lack a capability without breaking any of them. Ends with a line `Decision: ` naming the route, what the dev container or CI must add for it, and whether P-256 gets `encrypted-tpm`. If RSA cannot get `encrypted-tpm` without breaking the TPM for the kernel or systemd, the builder writes `BLOCKED.md` (RSA carries the RSA-PSS cases). Indexed in `docs/findings.md`.

features.title: Research: systemd 259 credential header and key identifiers
features.description: Settles the open question 'The credential identifiers for systemd 259'. `docs/findings/F153.md`, headed `## F153`, reads systemd's source at the exact version the Ubuntu 26.04 guest installs (from F151) and gives, with file and line: the layout of an encrypted credential's header (where the key identifier, the PCR mask and the TPM fields lie), and the identifier of each key a credential can carry: user-scoped 'host plus TPM' (the one the service's Varlink `Encrypt` gets when the daemon finds a usable TPM), host-only and its user-scoped form, TPM-only, the forms with a TPM public key, and the null key. It then makes real credentials with `systemd-creds` and `swtpm` in the dev container, as F110 did (one TPM-bound, one host-only, one bound to PCR 7, one with the null key), and shows each identifier and PCR mask read back from them, stating the systemd version that made each. Differences from the 257 and 262 values of `docs/findings/F110.md` are listed. Nothing is copied from the service's code. Ends with a line `Decision: ` naming how the harness reader makes its fixtures. Indexed in `docs/findings.md`.

features.title: Packages: the .deb depends on libtss2-rc0t64 and every package requires systemd 257
features.description: Design 4 and Design 5, packages. Design 4. `packaging/nfpm.yaml` makes the `.deb` depend (not recommend) on `libtss2-rc0t64`, next to the TPM2 Software Stack libraries it already declares, with a comment saying systemd loads `libtss2-rc` by `dlopen` and Ubuntu only recommends it. The `.rpm` and Arch package keep `tpm2-tss`, which ships every `libtss2` library. The dependency gate (`scripts/check-tss-deps.sh` / `scripts/check_tss_deps.py`, run by `just package`) requires `libtss2-rc0t64` in the `.deb`'s Depends and fails on a `.deb` that lacks it or only recommends it; its self-test `scripts/test-check-packages-deps.sh` gains those negative controls. The `.deb`'s `Pre-Depends` on systemd rises from 255 to 257 (the comment that cites ubuntu2404 is updated); the `.rpm` and the Arch package keep `systemd >= 257`. The package gate (`scripts/check-packages.sh`, run by `just package`) checks that each of the three formats requires systemd 257 or later, and fails on a package that has no systemd requirement or allows anything older; its self-test `scripts/test-check-packages.sh` gains a negative control per format (a fixture package allowing 255). The real-dpkg lifecycle test (`scripts/test-deb-lifecycle-real.sh`) gains a case where dpkg refuses the `.deb` on a root whose systemd is 255, with a message naming the systemd version; like every lifecycle test it runs at the checkpoint, not in this `verify`.

features.title: The credential client keeps only the user-scoped Varlink route

The service seals and opens credentials only through the user-scoped Varlink `Encrypt`/`Decrypt`, and keeps its header guard (nonzero PCR mask, null key, binding that does not match the kind) unchanged. No stored-credential migration is added (nothing is in use before M6). The `creds` integration tests pass with the 255 path gone, coverage and the CRAP gate hold over the code that remains, and no mutant survives on the changed lines.

features.title: The harness's own credential reader
features.description: Design 2. A reader in the end-to-end harness (`e2e/vm/credread.py`, Python like the other case helpers), sharing no code with the service and built from `docs/findings/F153.md`, not from `crates/`, reads a stored `systemd-creds` credential as root and prints its key identifier (by name) and PCR mask; with `--expect-tpm-bound` it exits 0 only for the user-scoped 'host plus TPM' identifier of the given systemd version with a zero PCR mask, and fails naming the reason for a host-only key, the null key, a nonzero PCR mask, an unknown identifier or a malformed header. features.title: Download and verify the Ubuntu 26.04 minimal cloud image
features.description: Design 1, image. A new recipe `just vm-image` (`e2e/vm/image.sh`) fetches the Ubuntu 26.04 minimal cloud image and Ubuntu's `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.gpg`, verifies the signature with `gpgv` against the Ubuntu cloud image keyring and the image against the signed checksum, and only then places it in a cache outside the repository (never committed); it prints the image serial and the checksum for the run record. A cached image is verified again before use. The pinning choice (one dated serial, or the current release image verified by signature; serial recorded either way) is recorded in `docs/decisions.md` with why. Its self-test `scripts/test-vm-image.sh`, joining `just test-scripts`, runs the script offline on local fixtures (a test key and signed sums) and shows it refuses a wrong checksum, a bad signature, a signature by another key, a missing sums file and a tampered cached image, leaving nothing in the cache.

features.title: VM launcher with its TPM modes: QEMU with KVM, OVMF, tpm-crb and swtpm, full and lacking
features.description: Design 1, machine. `e2e/vm/vm.sh` boots a verified image (F158) as an overlay, under QEMU with KVM, OVMF code and a per-run vars copy, and a `tpm-crb` device backed by an `swtpm` on the host whose state is fresh for each run and kept across guest reboots within it. It configures the guest on first boot with a cloud-init NoCloud seed and drives it over the channel of `docs/findings/F151.md` (run a command, copy a file in and out, wait for boot, power cycle with the `swtpm` state kept, shut down), changing nothing in the product. It refuses to start without a usable `/dev/kvm` (never software emulation) and cleans up QEMU, `swtpm` and its temporary files whatever the outcome. Its self-test `scripts/test-vm-launch.sh`, joining `just test-scripts`, runs it with stub `qemu-system-x86_64` and `swtpm` and checks the command lines (KVM, OVMF, `tpm-crb`, `swtpm` state directory reused across a power cycle and fresh per run), the seed contents, the refusal without KVM and the cleanup, each with a negative control. The launcher takes a mode: `full` (the virtual TPM unchanged) or `lacking` (the TPM made to lack a capability RSA 2048 needs by the route of `docs/findings/F152.md`, which changes the TPM as every guest process sees it and never the service alone). Anything else is refused before a VM starts. If F152's route needs a tool the dev container lacks, this feature adds it to `harness/Containerfile` first and writes `BLOCKED.md` for the rebuild, as F150. Its self-test `scripts/test-vm-modes.sh`, joining `just test-scripts`, checks with stubs the arguments each mode gives QEMU and `swtpm` (or the filter), that `full` adds nothing, that an unknown or missing mode is refused, and that `lacking` cannot start without its route in place, each with a negative control. The real boot runs at the checkpoint.

features.title: The VM case list and the VM run: just e2e-vm, install without recommends, the shipped unit and the record
features.description: Design 1, cases. The VM target has its own case list (`e2e/vm/cases.list`): the shared setup (install, service, users, key import), the groups `sign-*`, `noplain-*`, `pcr-*`, `fallback-*`, `tpm-clear-*` and `upgrade-kinds-*`, and the VM-only checks the later features add. The existing accounting (`e2e/check-cases.sh`) checks a VM run as it checks a container run: every case of the list reported exactly once, run or skipped, an unknown, missing or duplicated case failing the run. The cases M4 always reports skipped (`fallback-tpmbound-*`, `upgrade-kinds-tpmbound`) may be reported run only in a VM run and stay refused as run in a container run. Its self-test `scripts/test-e2e-vm-cases.sh`, joining `just test-scripts`, checks the list against the case scripts and the accounting with negative controls (missing, unknown, twice, a tpmbound case run in a container); the container skips self-test still passes. Design 1, product under test and record; acceptance 1 and 2. New recipes `just e2e-vm mode` (`full` or `lacking`) and `just e2e-vm-cases mode +names` (like `e2e-cases`) build the packages (`e2e-packages`), get the verified image (F158), boot it in the mode (F159), install the `.deb` with apt and `--no-install-recommends`, install the test tools (polkit test agent, `tpm2-tools`, `openssl`, the PKCS#11 consumers) in the guest only, run the shared setup and the selected cases with the existing guest scripts, and account for them (the case list above). VM-only cases: `/dev/tpmrm0` exists; `systemd-analyze has-tpm2` reports full support after the install; the install used no recommends; the installed unit is the shipped one with no drop-in and no `CUSTODIOD_TEST_SWTPM_TCTI`; the service reaches the TPM through `/dev/tpmrm0`. The run record, printed and saved under `target/e2e/`, names the target, the TPM mode, the image serial, the guest kernel, systemd, the package version, the `swtpm` version, `has-tpm2` in the guest and the time of each step. The VM target's time budget row is a person's (`budgets.tsv`). Its self-test `scripts/test-e2e-vm-host.sh`, joining `just test-scripts`, runs the driver against a stub VM and checks the steps, the `--no-install-recommends` install, the record fields and the failure paths, each with a negative control. The real run is at the checkpoint.

features.title: VM cases: the kinds in full and lacking mode, the credential's key, and the silent fallback
features.description: Acceptance 3, 4 and 5. In `full` mode, importing the RSA 2048 and the P-256 `.p12` gives kind `tpm` for both. In `lacking` mode, the RSA 2048 key gets `encrypted-tpm` in the import result, the API's list, `custodio list` and the import journal entry, and `custodio import` says the key is weaker and why (P-256 too, if F152's route allows it; otherwise P-256 is `tpm` and the case says so); `fallback-tpmbound-import` and `fallback-tpmbound-cli-list` run there and are not skipped. Every case that expects `encrypted-tpm`, in this and later features, reads the stored credential as root in the guest with the harness's reader (F157, `--expect-tpm-bound` for the guest's systemd version) and fails on a host-only or null key or a nonzero PCR mask. The fallback cases stay as they are in the containers (tpmbound reported skipped). Self-test `scripts/test-e2e-vm-kinds.sh`, joining `just test-scripts`, checks the expectations per mode with negative controls. Design 3, acceptance 11: A VM-only case of the `lacking` run hides `libtss2-rc` from systemd without removing the package (for example with `dpkg-divert`) and restarts what needs it; an import that the TPM's capabilities send to `encrypted-tpm` then fails with `CredentialsUnavailable`, its journal entry carries the `binding_mismatch` cause, the state directory holds nothing new, and no key of any kind exists for that id. With the library restored (and what needs it restarted), the same import gives `encrypted-tpm` and passes the reader (F157). The case restores the library whatever the outcome. Self-test `scripts/test-e2e-vm-silent.sh`, joining `just test-scripts`, checks the case's judgements with negative controls (an import that succeeds while hidden, a stored file, a missing cause, a key left under another kind).

features.title: VM cases: every mechanism signs with encrypted-tpm keys, RSA-PSS included, and no plaintext key
features.description: Acceptance 6. The `sign-*` cases run in the VM: each `encrypted-tpm` key signs through the PKCS#11 module with every mechanism the service offers for its type, including `CKM_RSA_PKCS_PSS` with each supported hash and the salt lengths 0, the hash length and the maximum, and every signature verifies in `openssl` with the key's certificate; `sign-kind-matches-mode` expects `encrypted-tpm` for RSA in `lacking` mode and `tpm` in `full`. Where a case script needs a VM form, the contract records the mapping. The container cases behave as in M4. `scripts/test-e2e-sign.sh` covers the VM expectations with negative controls. Acceptance 7. The `noplain-*` cases run in the VM: after each `encrypted-tpm` import, `scripts/check-no-plaintext.sh` finds no encoding of the private key in the state directory, and no unencrypted key file exists. The container cases behave as in M4. `scripts/test-e2e-noplain.sh` covers the VM expectations with negative controls.

features.title: VM cases: encrypted-tpm keys survive a PCR change, restarts, a TPM clear and an upgrade
features.description: Acceptance 8. The `pcr-*` cases run in the VM: after extending PCR 7 and another PCR and restarting the service, and again after a guest power cycle with the `swtpm` state kept (the VM form of 'restart `swtpm`', recorded in the contract's mapping), every `encrypted-tpm` key still signs. The container cases behave as in M4. `scripts/test-e2e-pcr.sh` covers the VM expectations with negative controls. Acceptance 9. The `tpm-clear-*` cases run in the VM with `encrypted-tpm` keys: after the TPM is cleared (the TPM's own clear command from the guest, or a fresh `swtpm` state, as the contract settles), signing fails with the documented error and a journal entry, and the key is still listed and can be deleted. The container cases behave as in M4. `scripts/test-e2e-tpmclear.sh` covers the VM expectations with negative controls. Acceptance 10. The `upgrade-kinds-*` cases run in the VM: package N and N+1 are both built from this tree (so N already depends on `libtss2-rc0t64`), and upgrading keeps each `encrypted-tpm` key, its owner, its certificate and its kind, and the key signs afterwards; `upgrade-kinds-tpmbound` runs there and is not skipped, and the credential still passes the reader (F157) after the upgrade. In the containers it stays skipped. `scripts/test-e2e-upgradekinds.sh` covers the VM expectations with negative controls.
